/api/task-guides/gf180mcuD.analog-db.tsn.title: Two-NMOS Temperature-Response Core

/api/task-guides/gf180mcuD.analog-db.tsn.description_html:
Self-Starting Isolated-Body PTAT Core Layout Task

Objective

Implement tsn_002_ptat_classic in GF180MCU D and submit self-contained GDS. The resistor-degenerated four-MOS source core has a positive temperature slope; candidate slope is measured and source-paired without a positive-slope acceptance bound. A maintained three-MOS startup branch establishes its operating state after power-up. Supply sensitivity remains: this is not a precision temperature reference or a calibrated thermometer.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.

Inputs and Interface

materials/circuit.cdl is the physical LVS authority; materials/circuit.spice is its simulator representation. materials/startup.spice and materials/temperature.spice define stimuli and observations. This problem is the description input. Ordered ports are vdd vout vss: supply, temperature-dependent output and return.

Retain all device dimensions, multiplicities and four-terminal connections. The 8/1 um core NMOS has both source and body on vout; its body must remain isolated from VSS. The physical primitive MM0 ... nfet_03v3_dn maps to XM0 ... nfet_03v3 in the simulator, with the same D/G/S/B and W/L/m. Use an isolated P-well inside a supply-tied deep N-well, with explicit N-well enclosure and physical well/substrate contacts. Extraction must retain the separation between the output body and substrate return. No body-to-VSS substitution is permitted. The core resistor is physical 1 kohm/square poly, W=2 um, L=40 um, nominal 20 kohm.

The added startup devices have W/L of 0.42/20 um (weak PMOS pull-up), 2/0.28 um (NMOS detector) and 0.42/1 um (NMOS injector). The detector reduces the startup control voltage after bias is established, turning off the injection path. The weak pull-up/detector branch still draws static current; all DUT supply power is measured. Preserve this branch as part of the DUT. Placement, routing, splitting and source/drain interchange are permitted only where accepted by the declared LVS equivalence rules. No statistical matching or placement style is scored. External stimulus and the output load belong to the testbench and must not be placed inside the DUT.

Operating Conditions

Use typical GF180 3.3 V MOS and poly models with statistical variation disabled. VSS is 0 V. Evaluate all 18 combinations of VDD = 2.7/3.0/3.3 V, temperature = -20/27/100 C and supply rise time = 0.1/10 us. Each startup condition measures its DC operating point at the selected supply and temperature. Independently sweep -20 to 100 C in 1 C steps once per supply; this sweep is independent of the startup temperature and supply-rise time. All three complete temperature sweeps and all 18 startup conditions are retained. The external output capacitance is exactly 100 fF.

For startup, ramp VDD linearly from 0 to its selected value, then hold it. Use a zero-initial-state uic transient through 100 us with no internal initial-condition bias or auxiliary startup source. Gear order 2 and a maximum timestep of 1 ns are declared. Measure final error, ripple and average power over 90–100 us. Startup time is the last falling crossing of the absolute output error through 1 mV, relative to that condition's DC operating point. This threshold-crossing measure is scored source-relatively and has no hard maximum-time limit; overshoot remains represented only by the declared finite-window error/ripple measurements.

The unipolar output must stay within the declared 0 to 3.3 V supply envelope, and this powered core must consume supply energy. Absolute errors, voltage ranges and startup times must represent their nonnegative measurement domains. These requirements have explicit rationales in case.toml; positive error, startup time and power remain scored quality objectives without upper rejection budgets. Missing or unusable measurements remain evaluation errors.

Physical Requirements

Submit top cell tsn_002_ptat_classic, all named electrical ports, resolved hierarchy and at most 10 MiB. Artifact, GF180 variant-D DRC including antenna, strict named-port LVS and geometry must pass with no DRC waivers. Chip-level density and seal-ring closure are outside this standalone-block scope.

The functional bounding box must fit within 220 by 65 um. Its area includes all declared device and routing drawing layers: wells (including deep N-well and isolated P-well), implants, active, poly, contacts, metals/vias and device markers. Annotation and pin-purpose shapes are excluded. All functional routing must use drawing layers. /protocol/task.json freezes the layer set.

Independent candidate extraction retains MOS and resistor geometry and adds distributed wiring RC. All scored simulation consumes that extracted DUT. This does not include a distributed silicon substrate model. Larger output loads are unqualified and can cause oscillation; this is not a pF-load output buffer. Brownout/restart, arbitrary supply ramps, process/statistical corners, noise, absolute temperature accuracy, supply rejection, EM and fabrication signoff are outside scope.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. Parasitic extraction is also mandatory: it must produce a complete, electrically consistent netlist usable by the required post-layout simulations. A completed candidate rejection scores zero; infrastructure errors do not establish candidate failure.

For layout scoring, cap every positively weighted raw quality at 1 before aggregation; the score ranges from 0 to 100. Reaching every weighted target scores 100, and no minimum score is required for validity.

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations remain required evidence. The explicit quality targets below supply scoring anchors; otherwise the paired source value is used. Reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the declared quality target, or the same-condition source measurement when no target is declared:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. First compute each metric's raw quality q from the worst paired condition, with raw area quality q_area = area_target / candidate_functional_area. Credit c_i = min(1, q_i) for every positively weighted metric, then compute S = 100 * product(c_i ** w_i). The weights sum to 1 and the score is bounded by 100. An improvement beyond one target cannot compensate for missing another target. Physical, extraction, or functional rejection scores zero; other missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Reaching every positively weighted target scores 100; a feasible reference may score far below 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs, not acceptance bounds.

For metrics declaring saturating_ratio, q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2*s), using the quality anchor b and the positive scale s in the metric’s units. Equality to the anchor gives raw quality 1; improvements approach raw quality 2 but credited quality stays at 1. Normalize each condition before selecting the worst quality. These scales and targets do not add acceptance cutoffs.

The capability coefficient is 6, independent of this task's reference-normalized score.

Quality targets and weights

The area quality target is 300 um2. It is an integration budget, not a hard limit or a proven process minimum.

The 300 um2 integration budget carries 50% for this fixed-device PTAT core. Curvature carries 20%. The worst paired mean/minimum/maximum temperature slope is scored as one 15% group with a 10 uV/C deviation scale, avoiding three correlated rewards for the same transfer law. Startup time carries 10% and peak power 5%. The 2 mV curvature budget over -20 to 100 C is close to the 1.9 mV worst source curvature. Repeated endpoint voltages, final ripple and repeated steady power observations remain diagnostics; fixed topology is not presented as freely tunable temperature compensation.

slope_profile takes the worst source-paired target quality across the mean, minimum and maximum temperature slopes, with a 10 uV/C deviation scale. The three original metrics retain their functional checks and observations with zero individual weights. This group carries 15% once, independently of the 20% curvature objective.

slope_profile paired source V/C 1e-05 0.15

Zero-weight observations: maximum_slope, minimum_slope, slope_v_per_c, ripple_v, startup_error_v, cold_v, hot_v, output_v, final_power_w, power_w. Original functional requirements remain enforced; grouped metrics listed above carry their stated weight once.

The judge independently extracts distributed wiring resistance and capacitance from the submitted GDS, retaining candidate-derived MOS/passive geometry and external body connections. Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. sections.Objective:
Implement the fixed tsn_003_ptat_4t_xcoupled circuit in GF180MCU D and submit self-contained GDS. Two NMOS and two PMOS devices form a resistorless temperature-dependent voltage core with cross-coupled bias connections. The fixed GF180 sizes are retained. The output increases with temperature under each declared supply, but both voltage and slope depend strongly on supply. This is a temperature-slope layout task, not a precision reference or calibrated thermometer.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. sections.Operating Conditions: Use the typical GF180 3.3 V MOS models and physical poly models where present, with statistical variation disabled. Unless swept explicitly, temperature is 27 C. VSS = 0 V; VDD = 2.7, 3.0 and 3.3 V. Measure the operating point at 27 C, then sweep temperature from -20 to 100 C inclusive in 1 C steps at each supply. The output is unloaded except for the measurement probe. No ideal internal source or passive is added.
sections.Physical Requirements:
Submit top cell tsn_003_ptat_4t_xcoupled with every named electrical port, resolved hierarchy and a file size at most 10 MiB. The judge independently extracts distributed wiring resistance and capacitance from the submitted GDS, retaining candidate-derived MOS/passive geometry and external body connections. Eight-Bit R-2R DAC Core Layout Task

Objective

Implement r2r in GF180MCU variant D while preserving the supplied circuit, device dimensions and ordered interface. Eight-bit passive voltage conversion with ideal external bit drivers and a 1 pF output load; ten transient codes plus the complete static 256-code transfer.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.

Inputs and Interface

Inputs are this description, materials/circuit.spice (the authoritative circuit) and materials/testbench.spice (stimuli and measurements). Runtime task metadata supplies consistent frozen constraints, evaluation conditions and output declarations.

Ordered subcircuit and GDS interface: b7, b1, b0, b2, b3, b4, b5, b6, out, VGND. b0–b7: ideal-driver bit inputs (b0 is LSB); out: analog output; VGND: substrate and ladder return.

Preserve topology, total device widths, channel lengths, multiplicities, resistor dimensions and body connections. Equivalent hierarchy, diffusion sharing and parallel fingers are allowed when connectivity and electrical checks pass; preserve source models and dimensions without idealizing internal devices. Retain dummy devices even when all their terminals are shorted.

Operating Conditions

Use 3.3 V bit-driver levels and 27 C, with 1 pF from out to VGND. For the two late transient accuracy samples, evaluate codes 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 and 255 separately. bit0 is the least significant bit. Each bit starts at 0 V and changes from 10 ns to 10.1 ns to 3.3bitN V. Simulate through 2 us with a 1 ns requested step. The expected settled voltage is 3.3code/256 V. Separately, a single static DC sweep maps codes 0 through 255 in 1-code steps to ideal 0/3.3 V bit levels and measures the complete settled transfer. This static sweep has no input transitions and makes no dynamic code-glitch claim. The external drivers and load are testbench components, outside the required passive circuit.

Use reviewed typical primitive models with statistical variation disabled. Numerical parameters from runtime simulation jobs generate the testbench's parameters.spice; interpolation and detailed PWL follow the delivered deck. Scope is limited to nominal compact-model conditions, excluding temperature/process corners, mismatch yield, noise, RF/EM and full-chip density closure.

LVS checks topology, dimensions, body terminals and all named top-level ports, case-insensitively. Electrical Requirements and Scoring

A completed candidate rejection scores zero; infrastructure errors do not establish candidate failure.

For layout scoring, cap every positively weighted raw quality at 1 before aggregation; the score ranges from 0 to 100. Reaching every weighted target scores 100, and no minimum score is required for validity.

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. Parasitic extraction is also mandatory: it must produce a complete, electrically consistent netlist usable by the required post-layout simulations. A completed candidate rejection scores zero; infrastructure errors do not establish candidate failure.

For layout scoring, cap every positively weighted raw quality at 1 before aggregation; the score ranges from 0 to 100. Reaching every weighted target scores 100, and no minimum score is required for validity.

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations remain required evidence. The explicit quality targets below supply scoring anchors; otherwise the paired source value is used. Reports retain every paired result.

/api/task-guides/gf180mcuD.voidwalkers-s.description_html:
Scan D Flip-Flop with Active-Low Reset Layout Task

Objective

Implement gf180mcu_voidwalkers_sc_sdffrnq_4 in GF180MCU variant D while preserving the supplied circuit, device dimensions and ordered interface. Functional data and scan selection, rising-edge storage, asynchronous active-low reset, and 50 MHz operation with 50 fF load.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.

Inputs and Interface

Inputs are this description, materials/circuit.spice (the authoritative circuit) and materials/testbench.spice (stimuli and measurements). Runtime task metadata supplies consistent frozen constraints, evaluation conditions and output declarations.

Ordered subcircuit and GDS interface: S, VDD, Q, B, CLK, A, RN, VSS. VDD/VSS: supply/return; A: functional data; B: scan data; S: select (0=A, 1=B); CLK: rising-edge clock; RN: active-low asynchronous reset; Q: stored output.

Preserve topology, total device widths, channel lengths, multiplicities, resistor dimensions and body connections. Equivalent hierarchy, diffusion sharing and parallel fingers are allowed when connectivity and electrical checks pass; preserve source models and dimensions without idealizing internal devices. Retain dummy devices even when all their terminals are shorted.

Operating Conditions

Use 3.3 V and 27 C, a 50 fF Q load and the same 50 MHz clock throughout (first rise 10 ns, rise/fall 0.1 ns, high time 10 ns). Select A initially; select B at 40.1 ns; return to A at 80.1 ns. A rises at 20.1 ns, falls at 60.1 ns, rises at 100.1 ns and falls at 120.1 ns. B rises at 60.1 ns. RN starts low, releases at 5.1 ns, asserts at 85.1 ns and releases at 95.1 ns. All data/reset transitions take 0.1 ns, as specified in the testbench.

The testbench also checks two late-cycle A-to-Q cases at the nominal 50 MHz clock and 50 fF load. At each measured rising edge, A crosses 1.65 V 0.8 ns before the edge and makes the opposite transition 0.2 ns after it, exercising setup and hold behavior. It checks Q after the capture edge and source-pairs the corresponding clock-to-Q delay and output slew. These fixed setup/hold exercises do not measure minimum setup/hold time or establish timing signoff across corners. Simulate through 200 ns.

Use reviewed typical primitive models with statistical variation disabled. Numerical parameters from runtime simulation jobs generate the testbench's parameters.spice; interpolation and detailed PWL follow the delivered deck. Scope is limited to nominal compact-model conditions, excluding temperature/process corners, mismatch yield, noise, RF/EM and full-chip density closure.

Physical Requirements

Submit a nonempty GDS with top cell gf180mcu_voidwalkers_sc_sdffrnq_4, no larger than 10485760 bytes. The functional bounding box must fit within 80 × 80 um and includes relevant device and routing polygons, implants/wells, passive markers, contacts, vias and dummy routing. The complete layer/datatype set is:

[[5,0],[11,17],[11,39],[12,0],[13,17],[21,0],[22,0],[22,4],[24,0],[24,5],[30,0],[30,4],[31,0],[32,0],[33,0],[34,0],[34,3],[34,4],[34,5],[35,0],[36,0],[36,3],[36,4],[36,5],[37,0],[38,0],[40,0],[41,0],[42,0],[42,3],[42,4],[42,5],[46,0],[46,3],[46,4],[46,5],[49,0],[53,0],[53,3],[53,4],[53,5],[55,0],[62,0],[75,0],[80,5],[81,0],[81,3],[81,4],[81,5],[82,0],[86,17],[88,17],[96,1],[100,5],[100,7],[100,8],[108,5],[110,5],[110,11],[110,12],[110,13],[110,14],[110,15],[110,16],[111,5],[112,1],[115,5],[116,5],[117,5],[117,10],[118,5],[119,5],[122,5],[123,5],[124,5],[125,5],[127,5],[128,17],[137,5],[151,5],[152,5],[153,51],[166,5],[167,5],[173,5],[178,0],[183,0],[184,0],[185,0],[204,0],[210,0],[220,0],[226,0],[227,0],[241,0]].

Area excludes text and nonfunctional boundary layers 0/0 and 63/0; functional geometry must remain on functional layers. Pass the fixed GF180 D FEOL, BEOL, connectivity, grid and antenna checks without waivers. Use five metal layers, the 1.1 um top-metal option and the 1 kOhm/square high-resistance poly option. Chip density and seal-ring closure belong to higher-level integration.

LVS checks topology, dimensions, body terminals and all named top-level ports, case-insensitively. Physically implement supply and substrate/well contacts; do not short different nets through adjoining silicided diffusion. After validity and geometric checks pass, extract candidate devices and distributed interconnect RC, then simulate the extracted circuit. The substrate model is one equipotential body region with explicit well/body contacts, rather than a distributed silicon-substrate network. Unreliable extraction, missing ports or incomplete measurements cannot establish success.

The standard-cell functional frame has fixed height 6.35 um and width on a 0.005 um grid. Coordinates below are relative to its lower-left functional bound; global translation remains allowed. Supply rails must be continuous on metal1 and bound by LVS to the named supply.

  • VDD: centre y = 6 um, thickness at least 0.23 um, from left + 0 um to right − 0 um.
  • VSS: centre y = 0.35 um, thickness at least 0.23 um, from left + 0 um to right − 0 um.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. Parasitic extraction is also mandatory: it must produce a complete, electrically consistent netlist usable by the required post-layout simulations. A completed candidate rejection scores zero; infrastructure errors do not establish candidate failure.

For layout scoring, cap every positively weighted raw quality at 1 before aggregation; the score ranges from 0 to 100. Reaching every weighted target scores 100, and no minimum score is required for validity.

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations remain required evidence; the quality targets below set the scoring anchors without depending on the submitted GDS. Reports retain every source/candidate pair.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the declared quality target, or the same-condition source measurement when no target is declared:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. First compute each metric's raw quality q from the worst paired condition, with raw area quality q_area = area_target / candidate_functional_area. Credit c_i = min(1, q_i) for every positively weighted metric, then compute S = 100 * product(c_i ** w_i). The weights sum to 1 and the score is bounded by 100. An improvement beyond one target cannot compensate for missing another target. Physical, extraction, or functional rejection scores zero; other missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Reaching every positively weighted target scores 100; a feasible reference may score far below 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs, not acceptance bounds.

propagation_delay Worst paired quality over the five existing data/scan/reset arcs and two additional A-data clock-to-Q arcs with 0.8 ns setup. s minimize / ratio 0 … +∞ —
output_transition Worst paired quality over the five existing data/scan/reset arcs and the two additional A-data output-slew arcs with 0.8 ns setup. s minimize / ratio 0 … +∞ —
supply Average VDD power over 20–200 ns, including the late-cycle timing stimuli. W minimize / ratio 0 … +∞ 1e-12

The area scoring target is 100 um2. It is a continuous quality goal, not a hard limit, process minimum or a percentage of the current feasibility witness.

  • propagation_delay: 5.5e-10 s. Keep all declared clock/data/reset-to-Q timing observations within 550 ps at 50 fF, including the late-cycle capture exercises.

The 100 um2 area goal rewards compact latch, clock and scan-multiplexer placement. Area carries 50%, worst source-paired propagation delay 40% and supply power 10%. Output slew remains diagnostic. The 550 ps timing goal, both fixed setup/hold exercises, scan selection and asynchronous reset remain checked.

Quality targets do not impose additional functional cutoffs. Metrics without an explicit target retain their same-condition source anchors.

The capability coefficient is 5, independent of this task's reference-normalized score.

Standard-cell design guidance

You may plan device rows, supply rails and signal access before routing. Represent pull-up/pull-down connections as transistor-edge graphs and explore compatible Euler paths and alternative orders to share diffusion and reduce breaks. Choose a legal arrangement considering routing length, parasitics and signal access. Keep fixed netlist sizes, models and connections; do not optimize sizing.

Use the declared row height, grid and supply-rail geometry. Keep local routing compact and signal pins accessible, avoiding routing layers with no benefit. Check DRC and named-port LVS, then extract the candidate and compare transitions in both directions and power against source simulation; iterate using parasitic measurements. These methods are optional and do not prescribe an algorithm or reference layout.

These methods refer to Sections 2–3 of Xu et al., Standard Cell Library Design and Optimization Methodology for ASAP7 PDK (https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.11396). Its FinFET sizing, track count and process-specific dimensions do not apply to this task.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. Parasitic extraction is also mandatory: it must produce a complete, electrically consistent netlist usable by the required post-layout simulations. Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance.   • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.

transition_s s Worst output 10–90% or 90–10% transition 0 to unbounded response: ratio, minimize, scale=1e-12

Five-Transistor OTA Core with Bias Mirror Layout Task

Objective

Implement the fixed six-MOS amp_001_5t circuit in IHP SG13G2 and submit a self-contained GDS. The circuit consists of a five-transistor OTA core and a sixth, diode-connected bias-reference MOS. Device dimensions are fixed.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.

Inputs and Interface

materials/circuit.cdl is authoritative for physical LVS; materials/circuit.spice is its simulator representation. materials/testbench.spice defines the AC/DC measurements. Port order is vdd vout vinp vinn ibias vss: supply, single-ended output, non-inverting input, inverting input, reference-current input, and return. Supply 20 uA from vdd into ibias; it is not an ideal voltage-bias input.

The NMOS input pair has W/L = 10/10 um; the PMOS mirror pair 10/7 um; the NMOS tail and reference devices 3.8/1 um, all with multiplicity 1. The CDL also declares substrate and well taps. Retain all electrical connections, body connections, sizes and tap devices. Placement and routing are free; normal source/drain equivalence and electrically equivalent device splitting are allowed only when the declared LVS checks accept them. No additional common-centroid or statistical matching requirement is scored.

Operating Conditions

The pinned mos_tt/res_typ models run at 27 C, with VDD = 1.5 V, VSS = 0 V, 20 uA reference current, 0.8 V non-inverting input bias, and an external 10 pF output load. The 4 GH/4 GF feedback network closes the DC loop and opens the AC loop. It is testbench apparatus, not part of the submitted layout. AC sweeps 1 Hz to 100 MHz at 100 points per decade. The power measurement includes the reference-current branch supplied from VDD. The 1e12 ohm numerical shunt is part of the declared simulation setup.

Physical Requirements

Submit top cell amp_001_5t, with all six named electrical ports, no unresolved hierarchy, and at most 10 MiB. Artifact, DRC, strict named-port LVS and geometry checks must pass. DRC uses the pinned main and extra/maximal rules without waivers; density and antenna are outside this standalone-block scope.

The functional bounding box must fit within 120 by 70 um. Its area includes all process device and routing drawing layers enumerated in the published runtime constraints, including wells, taps, implants, active, poly, contacts, all routing metals/vias and passive/device markers. Annotation text and pin-purpose shapes are excluded from area; functional routing must use drawing layers.

The judge extracts distributed RC from the submitted GDS and simulates that extracted DUT. Physical LVS retains explicit taps. Magic models the body connection through its extracted network without the separate compact ptap1 and ntap1 devices; source calibration records the effect of this boundary. This task covers nominal deterministic AC/DC behavior, not statistical mismatch, PVT, noise, distortion, transient settling, EM or manufacturing signoff.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. Parasitic extraction is also mandatory: it must produce a complete, electrically consistent netlist usable by the required post-layout simulations. A completed candidate rejection scores zero; infrastructure errors do not establish candidate failure.

  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Physical, extraction, or functional rejection scores zero; other missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Matching source-circuit performance at the reference area scores 100 points; each metric is capped at quality 1, so scores cannot exceed 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs rather than hard bounds.

The measurements below use the supplied SPICE node and source names. v(n) is a node voltage; i(V) is current flowing into a voltage source, so delivered power uses a negative sign. db(z)=20*log10(abs(z)); mag/abs denote magnitude, and cph denotes continuous phase in radians. find, when, from/to and rise/fall follow the deck's interpolation, window and crossing conventions. SPICE suffixes p/n/u/m/meg/g mean pico/nano/micro/milli/mega/giga. Nested avg, min, max, vecmin/vecmax and deriv represent window averages, extrema and sampled derivatives. Here margin is the total allowance across both sides, and the envelope sum is displayed to four decimal places. MOS/passive envelopes use W/L (or resistor dimensions) and multiplicity, including explicit contacts and HBT emitter/contact envelopes. Current-Buffer and Active-Feedforward OTA Layout Task

Objective

Lay out amp_002_alfio_raffc with its physical compensation and fixed transistor network, for the declared loop response and sustained unity-feedback step recovery.

The folded PMOS-input stage drives net050; a PMOS common-source stage drives net013, then a PMOS stage and NMOS mirror at net043 drive the output NMOS. An active feedforward path drives the output PMOS directly from net050. One capacitor connects output to net063, the source side of the first-stage NMOS cascode; the second connects net050 to net013. The current-buffer compensation terminal and the additional active path are real connection differences from the dual-capacitor and shared-resistor representatives. This case is not counted from a changed circuit name or size.

The maintained circuit retains all 24 source MOS groups as 89 physical fingers, 4 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. MOS W/L are rounded to the nearest 0.01 um process grid. The original W=18/20/30 um devices use 2×9/2×10/3×10 um parallel fingers; the resulting short-width model behavior is calibrated independently. The source's 14.3293 uA sink is external through net1. Physical substrate and separate N-well contacts retain the input PMOS bodies at their common source net31, electrically separate from the VDD well. No internal ideal bias source or output servo is introduced. Capacitor values are rounded to physical geometry; every branch remains internal to the DUT.

Inputs and Interface

Input PMOS bodies retain the separate source-tied well; other PMOS bodies use the VDD well and NMOS bodies use the VSS substrate contact. Preserve device W/L/m, body connectivity, all internal branches and total multiplicities in the authoritative netlist. Native equivalent parallel fingers are allowed only when LVS and electrical requirements pass. Do not short distinct ports or create extra driven monitors.

Internal passive devices are listed below; external loads are declared separately:

  • c0: net063 → vout, 3 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 43.46 × 43.46 um; nominal total 8.520333 pF.
  • c1: net050 → net013, 1 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 36.515 × 36.515 um; nominal total 2.0058602 pF.

The first falling 0 dB crossing defines unity-gain frequency, and 180+phase(T) at that crossing defines phase margin. A missing crossing is an evaluation error.

VINP rises from 0.5 V to 0.7 V during 2–2.02 us and falls during 10.02–10.04 us, repeating every 16 us. • materials/circuit.cdl: authoritative native LVS circuit.
  • materials/circuit.spice: simulation circuit bound to the process models.
  • materials/testbench.spice: bias, AC injection and transient tests.

Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout net013. VSS is return, VDD is supply, VINN/VINP are inverting/noninverting inputs, VOUT is output, and net013 connects the external 3.15498 uA sink to VSS.   • c0: net049 → vout, 4 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 44.775 × 44.775 um; nominal total 12.05746 pF.

sections.Objective:
Lay out amp_005_hoilee_affc with its physical compensation and fixed transistor network, for the declared loop response and sustained unity-feedback step recovery.

The folded PMOS-input stage drives net050; a PMOS/diode/mirror stage drives net049, followed by the NMOS output stage. A parallel path drives the output PMOS directly from net050. One capacitor connects net049 to output. The other connects output to net1, the source terminal of an additional common-gate NMOS returning current to net050. Six additional MOS (XM59–XM64) form this biased current-buffer branch; these devices and the low-impedance compensation terminal distinguish it from direct Miller and shared-resistor compensation.

The maintained circuit retains all 30 source MOS groups as 276 physical fingers, 7 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. MOS W/L are rounded to the nearest 0.01 um process grid. All source multiplicities are retained. The maintained 3.15498 uA sink is external through net013. The external bias is deliberately calibrated to 0.3 times the source current; this is not an unchanged upstream operating point. Physical substrate and separate N-well contacts retain the input PMOS bodies at their common source net31, electrically separate from the VDD well. No internal ideal bias source or output servo is introduced. Capacitor values are rounded to physical geometry; every branch remains internal to the DUT.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.
sections.Operating Conditions:
Use typical MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C, VDD=1.2 V and the declared external bias. All three output loads, 5/10/20 pF, must pass. At DC, VINP=0.5 V and VOUT feeds back to VINN through a zero-volt measurement source. For AC, inject 1 V in series with the feedback connection and set VINP AC=0; the return ratio at the high-impedance MOS input boundary is T=-V(vout)/V(vm). Sweep 150 points per decade from 0.01 Hz to 100 MHz with continuous phase, without arbitrary correction of the low-frequency phase offset. The first falling 0 dB crossing defines unity-gain frequency, and 180+phase(T) at that crossing defines phase margin. A missing crossing is an evaluation error.

VINP rises from 0.5 V to 0.7 V during 2–2.02 us and falls during 10.02–10.04 us, repeating every 16 us. Simulate 0–18 us with second-order Gear, a maximum step of 2 ns, rshunt=1e12, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1e-14 and vntol=1e-8. Numerical shunt branches are not physical bias or startup devices. PVT, mismatch, noise, distortion, rail-to-rail operation, power-up and stability under arbitrary loads are outside scope.
sections.Physical Requirements:
Submit GDSII top cell amp_005_hoilee_affc, at most 10 MiB. Pass native IHP main/maximal DRC without waivers (standalone scope; density/antenna disabled), strict named-interface LVS with explicit taps and a 3300 × 140 um functional envelope. All functional device, contact and routing drawing layers listed in the runtime outline constraint contribute to bounding-box area; annotation and pin-purpose layers do not.

Post-layout simulation uses the candidate's Magic RC netlist, including physical MIM/poly devices and interconnect parasitics, with explicit handling of half-grid GDS import. Magic idealizes substrate/well contacts; source simulation retains finite contact models. Distributed substrate resistance, substrate noise and manufacturing signoff are outside scope.
sections.Tools and Submission:
Soft solve budget: 3 hours.

Discover inputs, resources and feedback through /protocol/task.json (including its resources field) and /protocol/harness.json. Use the provided IHP primitives and KLayout, Magic and ngspice. Write /workspace/output/final.gds, then submit explicitly through the runtime protocol. Host configuration, source records and reference layouts are not standard solver inputs.

Solve workflow

  1. Read the declared circuit and materials, /protocol/task.json for paths, constraints and reviewed resources, and /protocol/harness.json for capabilities and helper commands. Task inputs under /task and resources under /resources are read-only; construct the layout in /workspace with the declared tools. With layout MCP, paths and commands refer to the remote EDA workspace. Create your own implementation with real devices, interconnect and pins, using your own tool loop without delegating to other agents; reference layouts and author code are not solver inputs.
  2. Inspect resources.external before using external tools. Each command starts a fresh shell: when tool modules are declared, source /usr/share/Modules/init/bash and load the selected tool's modules; export its declared tool_environment settings in that same command. Repeat as needed and use batch or headless operation. Local manuals, command references, and release notes may be available within the declared EDA installation and PDK resource directories. Locate these resources through /protocol/task.json and consult the documentation for the installed tool version when diagnosing unfamiliar syntax or tool failures.
  3. Generate an initial candidate and submit a snapshot early. When process-feedback is available, check the current GDS with layout MCP check or python -I /protocol/process_check.py before the final submission. This runs the final evaluator's complete plan and returns engineering diagnostics and candidate measurements, without scores or normalized quality factors. Checks have no count limit and consume the same wall-clock budget. Inspect the physical and functional results and all scored metrics; successful tool execution alone does not establish requirement satisfaction. Read paginated diagnostics with report when using MCP. Local exploratory checks do not replace this complete check.
  4. Use the remaining time for measured improvements to the declared quality objectives. Identify the limiting scored metrics, make targeted layout changes, regenerate and check the candidate, and compare measurements with the previous candidate and the stated scoring targets and trade-offs. Preserve the best valid candidate and revert changes that worsen the overall objective. Repeat while time and useful improvements remain; passing validity checks alone is not a stopping condition.
  5. Stop optimization when the budget expires, all declared quality objectives are achieved, or measured trials support convergence. If stopping early, explain the changes tried, the metric comparisons and the remaining limitations. Track remaining time through session status. At soft-budget expiry, finish or cancel already-started work and submit immediately; do not start another command, check or optimization round. If an MCP execution is running, use poll with its execution_id and the returned next_offset as offset until completion, or cancel it and wait for it to stop.
  6. Finish or cancel outstanding work, restore your best candidate to the declared output path, and explicitly submit it before ending the session. With layout MCP submit, remove the /workspace/ prefix from output.path; with the container interface, run python -I /protocol/submit.py. Wait for the receipt: only the last accepted snapshot is judged, and writing a file alone is not submission. Acceptance confirms delivery; the framework independently evaluates validity and quality after the session.

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.title: Current-Buffered Compensation OTA

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Output-Controlled Auxiliary Compensation OTA Layout Task

Objective

Lay out amp_006_leung_dfcfc1, retaining the complete folded PMOS-input stage, three-stage signal path, direct output feedforward, and auxiliary compensation. The folded stage drives net050, which drives the output PMOS and the PMOS/diode/mirror path to net049. That node drives both the output NMOS and an auxiliary common-source NMOS whose drain is net1; a biased PMOS loads this auxiliary drain. C0 connects net050 to output, while C1 connects net049 to net1. The auxiliary branch therefore acts on the NMOS output control node. In contrast, the separate AMP007 case's auxiliary PMOS senses net050 and its compensation terminates at net2.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.

Inputs and Interface

  • materials/circuit.cdl: authoritative native physical device graph.
  • materials/circuit.spice: matching simulator representation with logical body nets.
  • materials/testbench.spice: public bias, bilateral AC and step measurements.

Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout net013. VSS is return, VDD supply, VINN/VINP the inverting/noninverting inputs, VOUT output, and net013 the external bias-sink connection. Input PMOS bodies connect to the separate net31 source-tied well; other PMOS use the VDD well and NMOS use the VSS substrate. Preserve all 26 MOS groups, W/L/m, body connections, and both internal capacitive branches. Native equivalent parallel fingering is allowed only when all physical and electrical checks pass.

MOS dimensions retain the declared grid adaptation. All capacitors are physical cap_cmim:

  • c0: net050 (top plate) to vout (bottom plate), 8 parallel 48.935 × 48.935 um MIM units.
  • c1: net049 (top plate) to net1 (bottom plate), 3 parallel 50.94 × 50.94 um MIM units.

These are internal compensation devices, distinct from the external load. The normalized source's 27.4754 uA bias is deliberately calibrated to 6.86885 uA, improving headroom and finite tracking at the declared signal levels. No ideal output servo or internal numerical damping element is added.

Operating Conditions

Use typical IHP LV MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C and VDD=1.2 V, with an external 6.86885 uA sink from net013 to VSS. Every combination of 5/10/20 pF output load and 0.5/0.7 V DC input must pass. A zero-volt source from VINN (vm) to VOUT closes unity feedback. VINP is AC ground. The two DC input levels independently check operating-point error and the complete sampled return ratio.

At the closed input/output boundary, inject a series AC voltage with zero parallel AC current, then zero series voltage and unit current into vm. Both injections retain the original circuit and loading. With first-run b=-I(VPROBE), d=V(vm) and second-run a=-I(VPROBE), c=V(vm), define delta=a*d-b*c and the bilateral return ratio T=(2*delta-a+d)/(1-2*delta+a-d) (Tian et al., Eq. 30). The deck exports both injections' voltages/currents for independent two-port admittance reconstruction. This is a finite external-loop measurement, not a certificate for every internal pole or a complete Nyquist proof.

Sweep 0.01 Hz–10 GHz at 300 points/decade. Use continuous phase starting on its natural low-frequency branch, without a phase-offset correction. Check both first and final descending unity crossings, minimum sampled abs(1+T), maximum absolute continuous phase of 1+T across the entire sweep, and maximum gain over 2–10 GHz. Missing crossings or invalid measurements are evaluator errors; both first and final phase margins must lie in [0, 180] degrees. Minimum return distance and return-phase excursion have only nonnegative domain bounds; high-frequency gain has no acceptance bound. These full-sweep observations affect continuous quality and do not establish a stability certificate.

For each condition, VINP's pulse starts at 0.5 V, rises to 0.7 V at 2–2.02 us and falls at 10.02–10.04 us, with a 16 us period. Transient uses its own pulse-start operating point, independently of the AC DC-input setting. Simulate 0–18 us with the KLU linear solver and Gear order 2, 2 ns maximum step, itl4=1000, rshunt=1e12, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1e-12, and vntol=1e-8. The numerical shunt is not a physical device. The maintained 1 pA absolute current tolerance is checked at 0.1 pA with tenfold tighter relative/voltage tolerances and a 1e13 ohm shunt. Initial experimental 10 fA/1 fA current tolerances produced excessive iteration cost in the extracted low-resistance network. This numerical-floor calibration preserves every electrical bound and all physical/parasitic elements; half-step and trapezoidal controls independently check the observable dynamics. PVT, mismatch, noise, distortion, supply startup, rail-to-rail operation and arbitrary-load stability are outside this contract.

Physical Requirements

Submit GDSII top cell amp_006_leung_dfcfc1, at most 32 MiB. Pass native IHP main/maximal DRC without waivers (standalone scope, density/antenna off), strict named-interface LVS with physically verified body connections, and a 6400 × 130 um functional envelope. Every device/contact/interconnect drawing layer listed in the runtime outline constraint contributes to area; annotation/pin-purpose layers do not. Labels alone do not establish electrical connectivity.

Post-layout simulation uses the submitted GDS's complete Magic RC, with physical MIM devices and interconnect resistances/capacitances. Half-grid import is explicit. Magic retains only Metal3 interface labels in its isolated extraction copy to avoid repeated internal well-name aliases, while native LVS checks the original GDS and its actual body-contact connectivity. No resistance/capacitance threshold omits small parasitics. Source simulation and extraction use the same logical body-net boundary. Distributed substrate resistance/noise and fabrication signoff remain unqualified. The long independent witness is a feasibility layout, not an area optimum.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. Parasitic extraction is also mandatory: it must produce a complete, electrically consistent netlist usable by the required post-layout simulations. A completed candidate rejection scores zero; infrastructure errors do not establish candidate failure.

For layout scoring, cap every positively weighted raw quality at 1 before aggregation; the score ranges from 0 to 100. Reaching every weighted target scores 100, and no minimum score is required for validity.

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Every electrical anchor is its paired pre-layout observation, measuring preservation of the fixed circuit's performance at that condition. Reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b its same-condition pre-layout measurement:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. First compute each metric's raw quality q from the worst paired condition, with raw area quality q_area = area_target / candidate_functional_area. Credit c_i = min(1, q_i) for every positively weighted metric, then compute S = 100 * product(c_i ** w_i). The weights sum to 1 and the score is bounded by 100. An improvement beyond one target cannot compensate for missing another target. Physical, extraction, or functional rejection scores zero; other missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Reaching every positively weighted target scores 100; a feasible reference may score far below 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs, not acceptance bounds.

The measurements below use the supplied SPICE node and source names. v(n) is a node voltage; i(V) is current flowing into a voltage source, so delivered power uses a negative sign. db(z)=20*log10(abs(z)); mag/abs denote magnitude, and cph denotes continuous phase in radians. find, when, from/to and rise/fall follow the deck's interpolation, window and crossing conventions. SPICE suffixes p/n/u/m/meg/g mean pico/nano/micro/milli/mega/giga. Nested avg, min, max, vecmin/vecmax and deriv represent window averages, extrema and sampled derivatives. Measure each operating condition independently, pair it with the source result under that condition, and take the worst paired quality within each metric group.

For metrics declaring saturating_ratio, q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2*s), using the quality anchor b and the positive scale s in the metric’s units. Equality to the anchor gives raw quality 1; improvements approach raw quality 2 but credited quality stays at 1. Normalize each condition before selecting the worst quality. These scales and targets do not add acceptance cutoffs.

Quality targets and weights

For a minimizing metric, additional loss is max(0, x-b); for a maximizing metric it is max(0, b-x). Degradation quality is q = s/(s+loss): loss equal to the declared budget halves that metric's quality, while matching or improving the paired source receives full credit. Normalize each condition before taking the worst quality. This formula does not change functional requirements.

The area quality target is 30000 um2. It is an integration budget, not a hard limit or a proven process minimum.

The eleven fixed MIM plates occupy 26941.7246 um2, or 89.8% of the 30000 um2 footprint objective, leaving 3058.2754 um2 for plate spacing, enclosures and interconnect. MOS and contact layers may share footprint with MIM only where native rules allow. The fixed area objective is unchanged.

Return-distance loss retains its 0.05 budget. Around the source distance of 0.8, this loss raises the sampled peak sensitivity 1/min(abs(1+T)) by about 7%. It measures sampled external-loop robustness, without certifying every internal loop. Gain and phase-margin diagnostics retain zero weight.

settling_time_s measures the tail of both step responses. For the rising step, measure from the ramp end at 2.02 us until the output enters and remains within 200 uV of high_v until 9.5 us; high_v is the mean over 9-9.5 us. For the falling step, measure from 10.04 us using 200 uV around low_v until 17.5 us; low_v is the mean over 17-17.5 us. The band is 0.1% of the commanded 0.2 V step, independent of each circuit's DC offset. Interpolate the last band-entry crossing linearly between native samples. An already settled response has zero duration. If the endpoint is outside the band, report the full observation duration (7.48 us up or 7.46 us down); this is a censored quality observation, not a functional rejection. Compare each direction and condition with its own pre-layout duration, then take the worst paired quality. The additional-loss budget is 20 ns, one declared input-ramp interval. This finite-window measure does not guarantee asymptotic convergence.

Power and DC tracking accuracy carry independent weights. The following units are the nominal pre-layout operating-point observations; all three loads share the same DC value. Both normalized quality anchors are independently measured in the same-condition pre-layout characterization and equal 1 at the declared nominal source. A loss budget of 0.05 therefore gives q = 0.05 / (0.05 + max(0, x/b - 1)) in the original physical observations: a 5% power or error increase halves that metric's quality. This expresses power and precision preservation for the fixed circuit; it introduces no absolute power or offset target and no acceptance cutoff. Improvements retain full credit.

The offset-independent response_time_s integral remains a diagnostic: integrate abs(v(vout)-high_v)/0.2 over 2.02-9.5 us and abs(v(vout)-low_v)/0.2 over 10.04-17.5 us. Its zero weight avoids counting the same dynamic behavior twice while the scored settling duration exposes a slow tail that an integral can conceal. DC accuracy is scored separately so settling to an inaccurate plateau is not sufficient for full overall quality.

The authoritative MOS input preserves the original logical groups, W/L/m and all four terminal nets. scoring.rationale: The eleven fixed MIM plates occupy 26941.7246 um2, or 89.8% of the 30000 um2 footprint objective, leaving 3058.2754 um2 of planar overhead for plate spacing, enclosures and interconnect. MOS and contact layers may share footprint with MIM only where native rules allow. The area objective remains a demanding integration budget, not a proven minimum or an acceptance bound. Area carries 30%, minimum sampled return-distance preservation 20%, worst bilateral 0.1%-of-commanded-step settling-time preservation 20%, DC power preservation 15% and DC tracking-error preservation 15%. Return-distance loss retains its 0.05 budget; around a source distance of 0.8, this loss raises sampled peak sensitivity by about 7%. Settling-time loss uses 20 ns, one declared input-ramp interval. Its 200 uV band is relative to each circuit's own late output plateau and is 0.1% of the commanded 0.2 V step. The finite observation window censors an unsettled response to the window duration without adding a quality rejection threshold. Power and tracking error use dimensionless units equal to their same-condition nominal source observations, independently remeasured in the frozen pre-layout characterization. Their 0.05 loss budgets penalize a 5% increase with half metric quality, expressing preservation of the fixed circuit's power and precision; matching or improving the paired source receives full credit. Raw watts, volts and the response integral remain diagnostics. Phase-margin, gain and high-frequency diagnostics retain zero weight. All electrical quality anchors are same-condition pre-layout observations. These budgets affect continuous quality only and do not claim complete internal-loop stability or asymptotic settling.

sections.Electrical Requirements and Scoring:
Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. Parasitic extraction is also mandatory: it must produce a complete, electrically consistent netlist usable by the required post-layout simulations. A completed candidate rejection scores zero; infrastructure errors do not establish candidate failure.

For layout scoring, cap every positively weighted raw quality at 1 before aggregation; the score ranges from 0 to 100. Reaching every weighted target scores 100, and no minimum score is required for validity.

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Every electrical anchor is its paired pre-layout observation, measuring preservation of the fixed circuit's performance at that condition. Reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b its same-condition pre-layout measurement:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. First compute each metric's raw quality q from the worst paired condition, with raw area quality q_area = area_target / candidate_functional_area. Credit c_i = min(1, q_i) for every positively weighted metric, then compute S = 100 * product(c_i ** w_i). The weights sum to 1 and the score is bounded by 100. An improvement beyond one target cannot compensate for missing another target. Physical, extraction, or functional rejection scores zero; other missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Reaching every positively weighted target scores 100; a feasible reference may score far below 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs, not acceptance bounds.

The measurements below use the supplied SPICE node and source names. v(n) is a node voltage; i(V) is current flowing into a voltage source, so delivered power uses a negative sign. db(z)=20*log10(abs(z)); mag/abs denote magnitude, and cph denotes continuous phase in radians. find, when, from/to and rise/fall follow the deck's interpolation, window and crossing conventions. SPICE suffixes p/n/u/m/meg/g mean pico/nano/micro/milli/mega/giga. Nested avg, min, max, vecmin/vecmax and deriv represent window averages, extrema and sampled derivatives. Measure each operating condition independently, pair it with the source result under that condition, and take the worst paired quality within each metric group.

For metrics declaring saturating_ratio, q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2*s), using the quality anchor b and the positive scale s in the metric’s units. Equality to the anchor gives raw quality 1; improvements approach raw quality 2 but credited quality stays at 1. Normalize each condition before selecting the worst quality. These scales and targets do not add acceptance cutoffs.

Quality targets and weights

For a minimizing metric, additional loss is max(0, x-b); for a maximizing metric it is max(0, b-x). Degradation quality is q = s/(s+loss): loss equal to the declared budget halves that metric's quality, while matching or improving the paired source receives full credit. Normalize each condition before taking the worst quality. This formula does not change functional requirements.

The area quality target is 30000 um2. It is an integration budget, not a hard limit or a proven process minimum.

The eleven fixed MIM plates occupy 26941.7246 um2, or 89.8% of the 30000 um2 footprint objective, leaving 3058.2754 um2 for plate spacing, enclosures and interconnect. MOS and contact layers may share footprint with MIM only where native rules allow. The fixed area objective is unchanged.

Return-distance loss retains its 0.05 budget. Around the source distance of 0.8, this loss raises the sampled peak sensitivity 1/min(abs(1+T)) by about 7%. It measures sampled external-loop robustness, without certifying every internal loop. Gain and phase-margin diagnostics retain zero weight.

settling_time_s measures the tail of both step responses. For the rising step, measure from the ramp end at 2.02 us until the output enters and remains within 200 uV of high_v until 9.5 us; high_v is the mean over 9-9.5 us. For the falling step, measure from 10.04 us using 200 uV around low_v until 17.5 us; low_v is the mean over 17-17.5 us. The band is 0.1% of the commanded 0.2 V step, independent of each circuit's DC offset. Interpolate the last band-entry crossing linearly between native samples. An already settled response has zero duration. If the endpoint is outside the band, report the full observation duration (7.48 us up or 7.46 us down); this is a censored quality observation, not a functional rejection. Compare each direction and condition with its own pre-layout duration, then take the worst paired quality. The additional-loss budget is 20 ns, one declared input-ramp interval. This finite-window measure does not guarantee asymptotic convergence.

Power and DC tracking accuracy carry independent weights. The following units are the nominal pre-layout operating-point observations; all three loads share the same DC value. The testbench retains raw watts and volts and additionally prints power_normalized = power_w / power_unit and output_error_normalized = output_error_v / error_unit:

0.5 V 0.0001147648164198 0.002777053659362
0.7 V 0.0001143276099613 0.002933579773495

These constants only define dimensionless measurement units. Both normalized quality anchors are independently measured in the same-condition pre-layout characterization and equal 1 at the declared nominal source. A loss budget of 0.05 therefore gives q = 0.05 / (0.05 + max(0, x/b - 1)) in the original physical observations: a 5% power or error increase halves that metric's quality. This expresses power and precision preservation for the fixed circuit; it introduces no absolute power or offset target and no acceptance cutoff. Improvements retain full credit.

The offset-independent response_time_s integral remains a diagnostic: integrate abs(v(vout)-high_v)/0.2 over 2.02-9.5 us and abs(v(vout)-low_v)/0.2 over 10.04-17.5 us. Its zero weight avoids counting the same dynamic behavior twice while the scored settling duration exposes a slow tail that an integral can conceal. DC accuracy is scored separately so settling to an inaccurate plateau is not sufficient for full overall quality.

sections.Objective:
Lay out amp_006_leung_dfcfc1, retaining the complete folded PMOS-input stage, three-stage signal path, direct output feedforward, and auxiliary compensation. The folded stage drives net050, which drives the output PMOS and the PMOS/diode/mirror path to net049. That node drives both the output NMOS and an auxiliary common-source NMOS whose drain is net1; a biased PMOS loads this auxiliary drain. C0 connects net050 to output, while C1 connects net049 to net1. The auxiliary branch therefore acts on the NMOS output control node. In contrast, the separate AMP007 case's auxiliary PMOS senses net050 and its compensation terminates at net2.

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. sections.Operating Conditions:
Use typical IHP LV MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C and VDD=1.2 V, with an external 6.86885 uA sink from net013 to VSS. Every combination of 5/10/20 pF output load and 0.5/0.7 V DC input must pass. A zero-volt source from VINN (vm) to VOUT closes unity feedback. VINP is AC ground. The two DC input levels independently check operating-point error and the complete sampled return ratio.

At the closed input/output boundary, inject a series AC voltage with zero parallel AC current, then zero series voltage and unit current into vm. Both injections retain the original circuit and loading. With first-run b=-I(VPROBE), d=V(vm) and second-run a=-I(VPROBE), c=V(vm), define delta=a*d-b*c and the bilateral return ratio T=(2*delta-a+d)/(1-2*delta+a-d) (Tian et al., Eq. 30). For each condition, VINP's pulse starts at 0.5 V, rises to 0.7 V at 2–2.02 us and falls at 10.02–10.04 us, with a 16 us period. Transient uses its own pulse-start operating point, independently of the AC DC-input setting. /api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Auxiliary-Stage Miller Compensation OTA Layout Task

Objective

Lay out amp_007_leung_dfcfc2 with its physical compensation and fixed transistor network, for the declared loop response and sustained unity-feedback step recovery.

The folded PMOS-input stage drives net050; the PMOS/diode/mirror path drives net049 and then the NMOS output stage. Direct feedforward drives the output PMOS from net050. A separate PMOS common-source branch has gate net050, drain net2 and an NMOS bias sink. C1 connects net050 to output; C2 connects net050 to net2, across the auxiliary stage. This compensation branch is distinct from output-to-current-buffer injection and from the net049-controlled auxiliary termination in the other cases.

The maintained circuit retains all 26 source MOS groups as 440 physical fingers, 10 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. All MOS dimensions/multiplicities are retained exactly. The maintained 20 uA sink is external through net1. The source bias-current value is retained. Physical substrate and separate N-well contacts retain the input PMOS bodies at their common source net31, electrically separate from the VDD well. No internal ideal bias source or output servo is introduced. Capacitor values are rounded to physical geometry; every branch remains internal to the DUT.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.

Inputs and Interface

  • materials/circuit.cdl: authoritative native LVS circuit.
  • materials/circuit.spice: simulation circuit bound to the process models.
  • materials/testbench.spice: bias, AC injection and transient tests.

Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout net1. VSS is return, VDD is supply, VINN/VINP are inverting/noninverting inputs, VOUT is output, and net1 connects the external 20 uA sink to VSS. Input PMOS bodies retain the separate source-tied well; other PMOS bodies use the VDD well and NMOS bodies use the VSS substrate contact. Preserve device W/L/m, body connectivity, all internal branches and total multiplicities in the authoritative netlist. Native equivalent parallel fingers are allowed only when LVS and electrical requirements pass. Do not short distinct ports or create extra driven monitors.

Internal passive devices are listed below; external loads are declared separately:

  • c1: net050 → vout, 5 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 47.61 × 47.61 um; nominal total 17.038429 pF.
  • c2: net050 → net2, 5 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 47.61 × 47.61 um; nominal total 17.038429 pF.

Operating Conditions

Use typical MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C, VDD=1.2 V and the declared external bias. All three output loads, 5/10/20 pF, must pass. At DC, VINP=0.5 V and VOUT feeds back to VINN through a zero-volt measurement source. For AC, inject 1 V in series with the feedback connection and set VINP AC=0; the return ratio at the high-impedance MOS input boundary is T=-V(vout)/V(vm). Sweep 150 points per decade from 0.01 Hz to 100 MHz with continuous phase, without arbitrary correction of the low-frequency phase offset. The first falling 0 dB crossing defines unity-gain frequency, and 180+phase(T) at that crossing defines phase margin. A missing crossing is an evaluation error.

VINP rises from 0.5 V to 0.7 V during 2–2.02 us and falls during 10.02–10.04 us, repeating every 16 us. sections.Objective:
Lay out amp_010_peng_acbc with its physical compensation and fixed transistor network, for the declared loop response and sustained unity-feedback step recovery.

The folded PMOS-input stage drives net050; a PMOS/diode/mirror stage drives net049, followed by the NMOS output stage. The output PMOS also receives feedforward drive from net050. C0 connects net050 to output, while C1 connects net049 to net1. The auxiliary node has a bias-fed PMOS, a diode-connected PMOS and an NMOS controlled by net043; this three-device branch creates a distinct active compensation termination. It is neither a second output-connected Miller capacitor nor the six-MOS current-buffer branch of the other representative.

The maintained circuit retains all 27 source MOS groups as 237 physical fingers, 6 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. MOS W/L are rounded to the nearest 0.01 um process grid. All source multiplicities are retained. The maintained 1.80825 uA sink is external through net013. The external bias is deliberately calibrated to 0.1 times the source current; this is not an unchanged upstream operating point. Physical substrate and separate N-well contacts retain the input PMOS bodies at their common source net31, electrically separate from the VDD well. No internal ideal bias source or output servo is introduced. Capacitor values are rounded to physical geometry; every branch remains internal to the DUT.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.
sections.Operating Conditions:
Use typical MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C, VDD=1.2 V and the declared external bias. All three output loads, 5/10/20 pF, must pass. At DC, VINP=0.5 V and VOUT feeds back to VINN through a zero-volt measurement source. For AC, inject 1 V in series with the feedback connection and set VINP AC=0; the return ratio at the high-impedance MOS input boundary is T=-V(vout)/V(vm). Sweep 150 points per decade from 0.01 Hz to 100 MHz with continuous phase, without arbitrary correction of the low-frequency phase offset. The first falling 0 dB crossing defines unity-gain frequency, and 180+phase(T) at that crossing defines phase margin. A missing crossing is an evaluation error.

VINP rises 0.5→0.7 V at 20–20.1 us and falls at 100.1–100.2 us, repeating every 160 us. Simulate 0–180 us with Gear order 2, 10 ns maximum step, rshunt=1e12, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1e-14, vntol=1e-8. The numerical shunt is not a manufactured bias or startup device. PVT, mismatch, noise, distortion, rail-to-rail operation, supply startup and arbitrary-load stability remain outside the contract.

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Peng IAC Three-Stage Amplifier Layout Task

Objective

Implement amp_011_peng_iac with the supplied fixed topology and dimensions. The PMOS input pair and cascoded branches feed voutn/voutp. The PMOS bias mirror is cascoded with vb2, generated by XM65/XM63/XM64. XM10 drives net043; XM67/XM68 and XM70 retain the auxiliary current path, with XM69 driving net10 against XM66. XM11/XM23 drive vout. Compensation retains 1.95593 pF between voutp and vout, and 4.33595 pF between net10 and net4 with 1.46466 Mohm from net4 to vss. Do not replace the circuit, delete compensation, or add a servo. The physical core contains 34 logical MOS groups with upstream multiplicities. Each PMOS input body remains tied to its own tail node through its physical well contact.

Optimization objective

Maximize the declared quality score within the solve budget while satisfying all physical and necessary functional requirements. The first passing DRC, LVS and required electrical checks establish a feasible baseline. Continue improving the scored metrics from that baseline; a passing check or task_success = true does not mean that the quality objectives have been achieved.

Inputs and Interface

materials/circuit.cdl is the physical authority; materials/circuit.spice is its matching simulator representation. materials/testbench.spice defines closed-loop observations and materials/ac.spice defines balanced differential AC excitation. Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout vb1. vss is ground, vdd supply, vinn/vinp negative/positive input, vout the single-ended output, and vb1 the external bias-current sink. Bias, input drivers, feedback wiring and load are external test apparatus; all internal R/C and actual body contacts are physical DUT elements.

Operating Conditions

IHP SG13G2, nominal TT/typical, 27 C, supply 1.5 V, input reference 0.24 V, external current sink 7.11568e-07 A to vss, and 10 pF output load. Use the fixed IHP LV binding at 1.5 V, adapting the authored 1.8 V stimulus to the LV process rail; retain its bias current and input reference. Round W/L to 10 nm so half-gate contacts remain on grid. The closed-loop deck ties vinn directly to vout, drives vinp with a +100 mV pulse starting at 2 us (100 ns rise/fall, 18 us high duration), and runs to 40 us with 2 ns maximum steps, Gear order 2, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1 pA, vntol=10 nV. A disconnected timing marker forces exact integration-window endpoints. Transient starts from the solved DC point; this is not a zero-state supply-ramp startup test. High and return windows are 15–20 and 35–40 us.

AC spans 1 Hz–1 GHz at 200 points/decade. The differential deck retains DC output feedback through a 1 GH inductor and AC-isolates its bias node with 1 kF to ground; vinp/vinn receive balanced +0.5/-0.5 V small-signal excitation. It verifies residual input common-mode amplitude <=1 uV and DC feedback mismatch <=1 uV. These are external small-signal bias fixtures, not physical compensation. Both decks use rshunt=1e12 ohm to regularize otherwise floating extracted nodes; this numerical conductance is applied equally to source and candidate and is not a DUT compensation branch. The separate closed-loop deck measures actual follower response. No voltage-transfer estimate is labeled a loop return ratio.

Physical Requirements

Supply a GDS <=64 MiB with top cell amp_011_peng_iac, within 20000 by 2000 um (the task's artifact-size/outline bounds). Native DRC, strict named-interface LVS and functional-area measurement must pass; no marker waivers apply. Preserve MOS dimensions, multiplicities, body connections, all physical R/C and logical body connectivity. Functional layers in the published task include active, implant, wells, gates, contacts, passive plates, vias and routing; annotation/text-only layers are excluded. IHP native main and maximal DRC use the pinned PDK block profiles, with chip-level density and antenna disabled. Native MIM and high-poly primitives retain their compact models. Magic idealizes well/substrate taps; source simulation uses the declared logical body connections. This is not distributed substrate or RF/EM extraction. Candidate-derived Magic distributed RC feeds every post-layout job.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Artifact, geometry, DRC, LVS and declared functional requirements must pass. Parasitic extraction is also mandatory: it must produce a complete, electrically consistent netlist usable by the required post-layout simulations. A completed candidate rejection scores zero; infrastructure errors do not establish candidate failure.

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. sections.Operating Conditions:

AC spans 1 Hz–1 GHz at 200 points/decade.
